items.stem: An NFT's metadata points to a normal web URL that later goes offline. What breaks?

options.text: The token still exists on-chain but its referenced media no longer resolves
options.rationale: Correct: on-chain ownership persists while off-chain media can disappear.
A dead link does not burn the token.

options.text: The blockchain deletes the owner record

options.rationale: A broken link does not drain funds.

items.explanation: Correct: on-chain ownership persists while off-chain media can disappear.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about NFT ownership are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Owning the token proves control of the on-chain registry entry for that ID
options.rationale: Correct: the token records on-chain ownership.

options.text: Owning the token does not by itself transfer copyright in the artwork
options.rationale: Correct: IP rights require a separate legal grant.

options.text: Owning the token guarantees the media is stored on-chain
Owning the token guarantees future royalties to the buyer
options.rationale: Royalties flow to the creator, not the buyer, and are not guaranteed.

items.explanation: Correct: the token records on-chain ownership.

items.stem: Why is decentralised, content-addressed storage preferred for NFT media meant to last?

options.text: The reference is tied to the content's hash, so the link does not silently change or rot
options.rationale: Correct: content addressing makes media verifiable and durable.

options.text: It stores the media directly inside the token for free
options.rationale: It stores off-chain but addressably, not inside the token.

options.text: It makes the NFT immune to all loss
options.rationale: Pinning still matters; it is not absolute.

options.text: It encrypts the art so no one can view it
options.rationale: It does not encrypt by default.

items.explanation: Correct: content addressing makes media verifiable and durable.
